content.text: This step adds three small exported git wrappers in `internal/gitutil`: one that lists every commit in base..head with its Entire-Checkpoint trailer values while keeping trailer-less commits so the report can say "no checkpoint" instead of silently dropping them, one that resolves a checkpoint id to its ref, and one that computes the merge base used as the default when no base flag is given. The design decision is to read checkpoint data through plain git commands (log with trailer formatting, for-each-ref, and later ls-tree and show) rather than importing the CLI's checkpoint packages, which keeps the plugin independent of the CLI module and preserves its no-network contract. The ref lookup deliberately matches `refs/entire/checkpoints/*/<id>` by glob so a future change to the shard scheme cannot break resolution, and it rejects ids containing path or glob characters before shelling out. The assumption verified against the CLI source is that the ref leaf is the full checkpoint id and that the checkpoint tree root holds a metadata.json alongside per-session directories.
